newsitem.title: USA: Sony eyes talent agent for studio job.
newsitem.headline: Sony eyes talent agent for studio job.

text.p: Arnold Rifkin, a top talent agent at William Morris, is in talks with Sony Corp. about taking over Sony's troubled motion picture business.

According to people familiar with the studio's plans, Rifkin was recently approached by Sony executives looking to replace Columbia TriStar Motion Pictures Co. chief Mark Canton, who has come under fire after several films performed poorly at the box office.
While terms of the deal still need to be worked out, including the status of Rifkin's contract at William Morris, sources said Rifkin and Sony could strike a deal soon.
A spokesman for Sony Pictures declined to comment on the talks, which were first reported Wednesday by Daily Variety.
Variety said Canton, who has two years remaining on his contract, is expected to forge a production deal with Sony. But industry sources said the studio may opt for a financial settlement instead.

Canton, formerly head of production at Warner Bros., was hired five years ago to replace Frank Price as chairman of Columbia Pictures. While Sony has had some success with films such as "The Net" and "Jumanji", other films, such as "The Cable Guy" have failed to live up to the studio's expectations, putting pressure on Canton because he agreed to pay Carrey $20 million to star in the picture.

In making the jump to Sony, Rifkin would be following in the footsteps of rival talent brokers Michael Ovitz and Ron Meyer, who left Creative Artists Agency for executive jobs at Walt Disney Co. and Seagram Co. Ltd's MCA Inc. respectively.
Known for using motivational techniques and metaphors to encourage his troops, Rifkin was brought in four years ago to revamp the agency's sputtering motion picture department.

During his tenure, Rifkin helped create a sense of professionalism at the agency, urging his agents to work in teams to sign major stars. The moves have paid dividends for William Morris with stars such as Sylvester Stallone, Whoopi Goldberg, Geena Davis and Charlie Sheen joining in the last few years.
Analysts say Rifkin's management style, coupled with his close relationship with some of Hollywood's top talent, should come in handy at Sony.
"I don't think you can emphasise the relationship side enough," said entertainment analyst Jeff Logsdon, of Cruttendon Roth. "It's one step closer to the source of talent."
Sony has been a source of considerable turmoil this summer following the disappointing box office results of "The Cable Guy" and "Multiplicity" and the departure of several key executives.

Last month, rumours were rampant that Sony was planning to replace Canton and Sony Pictures President and Chief Operating Officer Alan Levine. The studio took the unusual step of issuing a statement in support of Levine but it stopped short of assuring employees that Canton's job was secure.

The move is the latest in a series of executive changes at Sony. The studio recently replaced marketing chief Sid Ganis with former Disney executive Robert Levin and replaced TriStar president Marc Platt with HBO Pictures president Robert Cooper. Lisa Henson, head of Columbia Pictures, stepped down in July.
Sony, which acquired Columbia Pictures in 1989 for $3.4 billion, has had a hard time finding the right management team to make the investment work.

The Japanese electronics giant spent millions of dollars to hire Peter Guber, a producer whose credits include "Batman", and his friend Jon Peters, even though they had no experience running a major studio.

The move proved to be disastrous for Sony as the executives spent lavishly on projects and studio improvements but failed to boost Sony's fortunes at the box office. Guber eventually resigned in 1994, just before Sony took an embarrassing $3.2 billion write-off.

Levine, an entertainment lawyer, was brought in to restore order to Sony's operations and reduce costs. While he has certainly proved adept at cutting expenses, Sony has not had a major hit since the Robin Williams film "Jumanji" was released last year.
